description: Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a beloved Indian dish featuring tender chicken pieces swimming in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. This iconic curry is known for its mild spice, sweet undertones, and luxurious texture, making it a favorite worldwide. Perfect for a comforting meal, it pairs wonderfully with naan or rice.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon of Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon of garam masala, and salt. Mix thoroughly to coat the chicken evenly. Cover the bowl and let it marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate for 2-4 hours for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and the vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary, searing each side until lightly browned and partially cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the chicken from the pan and set it aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Makhani Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, reduce the heat to medium and add 1 tablespoon of butter. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it becomes translucent and soft, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the tomato puree, remaining 2 teaspoons of Kashmiri red chili powder, and salt to taste. Bring the mixture to a simmer.

instructions.title: Simmer and Soften Cashews
instructions.text: Cover the pan and let the tomato mixture simmer gently for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil begins to separate from the edges. Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the simmering sauce along with 1 cup of water. Stir well, cover, and cook for another 5-7 minutes to allow the cashews to soften completely.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce to Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the pan from the heat and let the sauce cool slightly. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender directly in the pot. Blend until the sauce is completely smooth and creamy. For an exceptionally silky texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on any solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low heat. Add the partially cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir in the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, the heavy cream, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of garam masala, and the crushed kasoori methi (rubbed between your palms to release its aroma). Add the sugar and adjust salt if needed. Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to finish cooking and absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot.

tips: For the silkiest sauce, blend it very thoroughly and then pass it through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any onion or cashew bits.
Kashmiri red chili powder provides vibrant color with less heat; if unavailable, use a mix of paprika and a pinch of cayenne.
Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: A Quintessential Indian Lunch Recipe

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian lunch recipe is a global favorite, renowned for its rich, creamy texture, tantalizing aroma, and perfectly tender chicken. Originating from the bustling kitchens of Delhi, Butter Chicken has transcended borders to become a beloved comfort food, gracing tables from casual family meals to elegant restaurant dinners. If you're looking to explore the vibrant world of Indian cuisine, mastering this classic dish is an absolute must. It’s a culinary journey that promises an explosion of flavors, making it an unforgettable addition to your cooking repertoire.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

The iconic Butter Chicken is a staple of North Indian cuisine, specifically Punjabi fare. Its full name, Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing its decadent nature. At its core, it features succulent pieces of chicken, traditionally marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried until slightly charred. These tender morsels are then simmered in a luscious, vibrant orange-red gravy made from tomatoes, butter, fresh cream, and a fragrant blend of aromatic spices like ginger, garlic, garam masala, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi).

The magic of Murgh Makhani lies in its exquisite balance of flavors. The tanginess of the tomatoes cuts through the richness of the butter and cream, while the spices add depth without being overtly spicy. It’s a dish that offers a symphony of sweet, savory, and subtly spicy notes, creating a profoundly satisfying culinary experience. Unlike some spicier Indian curries, Butter Chicken is known for its mild, approachable flavor profile, making it a crowd-pleaser for all ages and palates. Its smooth texture and rich taste make it a perfect centerpiece for any Indian lunch recipes spread.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

Preparing the perfect Butter Chicken requires a few key components. While the list might seem long, most ingredients are pantry staples in Indian cooking, ensuring a truly authentic flavor.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (or paprika for less heat)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani Gravy:
*   2 tbsp butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 cup tomato puree (from fresh tomatoes or canned)
*   1/4 cup cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, optional but recommended for creaminess)
*   1/2 cup water
*   1/2 tsp red chili powder
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1 tsp kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 tsp sugar (optional, to balance tanginess)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh coriander for garnish

## Step-by-Step Butter Chicken Instructions

Now, let's dive into making your own delectable Butter Chicken. Follow these steps for a restaurant-quality meal at home.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon of oil. Once the butter melts, add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
4.  **Add Aromatics and Tomatoes:** Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Pour in the tomato puree, soaked cashews (if using), and 1/2 cup of water. Bring to a simmer.
5.  **Season the Gravy:** Add the red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well. Cover the pan and let it simmer for 10-15 minutes on low heat, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to cook down. The oil should start separating from the mixture.
6.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve.
7.  **Finish the Makhani Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan. Stir in the crushed kasoori methi and sugar (if using). Bring to a gentle simmer.
8.  **Combine and Serve:** Gently fold in the cooked chicken pieces into the gravy. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream. Heat through for a couple of minutes, but do not boil after adding cream. Garnish with fresh coriander.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Mastering Butter Chicken isn't just about following a recipe; a few professional tricks can elevate your dish from good to extraordinary.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse it with flavor, making a significant difference in the final taste and texture of your Butter Chicken.
*   **Char the Chicken:** If possible, grill the marinated chicken over charcoal or cook it in a very hot pan until it develops some slight charring. This adds a smoky depth that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** A perfectly smooth gravy is crucial. If you don't have a high-speed blender, a regular blender followed by straining through a sieve will achieve that restaurant-quality texture.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste and adjust seasonings. The sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes, and a pinch of salt can brighten all the other flavors. Don't forget the kasoori methi – it's a non-negotiable ingredient for authentic taste!
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality butter and fresh, ripe tomatoes for the best flavor. Fresh cream is also essential for that signature richness.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, creating a complete and satisfying Indian lunch.

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, fluffy naan is the quintessential pairing, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a light, aromatic base that beautifully complements the creamy curry.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber or mint raita (yogurt dip) offers a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Murgh Makhani.
*   **Salad:** A simple side salad with sliced onions, tomatoes, and cucumbers can add a fresh crunch.
*   **Pickles:** A small side of Indian pickle can add a tangy, spicy kick that enhances the meal.

## Butter Chicken Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is universally loved, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary preferences or explore new flavor profiles.

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas for a delicious vegetarian alternative. Marinate paneer similarly to chicken for extra flavor.
*   **Less Spicy Version:** Reduce the amount of red chili powder or replace it entirely with paprika for a milder, sweeter flavor.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** Use coconut cream instead of heavy cream and a dairy-free butter alternative. Ensure your yogurt for marination is also dairy-free.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you can’t grill the chicken, a touch of liquid smoke or an onion charring technique (burning an onion half directly on a flame until black, then simmering it with the gravy base) can impart a subtle smoky essence.
*   **Different Proteins:** While chicken is traditional, you can also make this recipe with lamb, shrimp, or even fish, adjusting cooking times accordingly.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a dish; it's an experience. Its comforting warmth and exquisite flavors make it a standout among Indian lunch recipes. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook, making Butter Chicken is a rewarding experience that brings the authentic taste of India right to your kitchen. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to indulge in one of the world's most beloved curries.
